clue.text: Charge for popular safety device

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fuse is an electrical safety device that breaks a circuit

explanation.surface: A fee for a widely liked safety gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge something with a quality is to imbue or fill it, a synonym.

clue.text: Boundless as a Mariner's resource-and-sagacity? Just so

definitions.text: as a Mariner's resource-and-sagacity? Just so

explanation.surface: A sailor of limitless wit, from a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's Just So Stories, the whale story has a Mariner of infinite-resource-and-sagacity.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinite means without limit, and it is Kipling's word for the Mariner's resourcefulness.

clue.text: Anticipates everyone deserting these wooded areas

indicators.note: deserting means the everyone word leaves the longer word

parts.note: to forestall is to anticipate and prevent
all is everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone abandons the woods ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Large tree-covered tracts of land are forests, a definition by description.

clue.text: Donkey in crowd's upset initially by incendiary device

indicators.note: in means the donkey word sits inside the turned crowd word
upset, in a down clue, turns the word for crowds upside down

parts.note: mob's, read as mobs, is crowds
moke is British slang for a donkey

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A donkey in an upset crowd is hit by a firebomb.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the crowd word upside down; moke is everyday British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke bomb is a device that is set off to release smoke, here loosely called incendiary.

clue.text: Flight involving publicity stunt

indicators.note: involving means the word for flight wraps round the publicity letters

parts.note: flight is running away, an escape
an ad (advertisement) is publicity

explanation.surface: An aircraft trip with a publicity stunt on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring, unconventional exploit or prank is a stunt, a near synonym.

clue.text: Part of meal easily prepared for some students

explanation.surface: A quick lunch for students.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate of sandwiches makes an easy meal stage, and a sandwich course alternates study with work placements.

clue.text: Crime thus contained in a fighting force

indicators.note: contained in means the thus word sits inside the force

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
so means thus

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing kept within the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is an example of a crime.

clue.text: Good-humoured sailor entering a race

indicators.note: entering means the sailor goes inside the race

parts.note: the mile is a running race
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A cheerful seaman runs in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means friendly and pleasant, a synonym.

clue.text: It's burnt in Fife, perhaps, extremely gladly

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the place name is rearranged into another form
extremely takes the outer letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Something gleefully set alight in a Scottish county.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife is a Scottish county; FIFE rearranges to EFFI, then G and Y close it.
explanation.definitionFit: An effigy, a dummy of a hated figure, is traditionally burnt, as on Bonfire Night.

clue.text: Coach on course giving instructions to players

parts.note: a stage, as in stagecoach, is a coach
a direction is a course taken

explanation.surface: A sports coach gives his team instructions on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions in a script tell actors what to do, so are instructions.

clue.text: Relinquish tax-paid return, being out of one's mind

parts.note: to forgo is to give up or relinquish

indicators.note: return asks for the word for tax-paid to be read backwards

parts.note: nett, of income, means after tax has been paid

explanation.surface: Someone driven mad by giving up a tax return.
explanation.walkthrough: Nett (British spelling of net) describes income after tax is taken off; 'return' reads it backwards, not a tax return.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer remembered has gone out of one's mind, an idiom.

clue.text: Having difficulty in moving a corpse

explanation.surface: A dead body that is hard to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff describes rigid, aching limbs, and is also slang for a dead body.

clue.text: In the home, urge to make savings

parts.note: a nest is a home, especially a bird's
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: A domestic impulse to put money aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum of money put away for the future is a nest egg, an idiom for savings.

clue.text: Bletherer giving music-maker a preliminary puff

explanation.surface: A chatterbox blows into a musical instrument before playing.
explanation.walkthrough: The bag of the bagpipes is the wind bag, filled with a puff before the music starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome talker is a windbag, and a bagpipe's air reservoir is literally a bag of wind.

clue.text: Poet carried into a steamship

indicators.note: carried means the letters are held inside the outer word

parts.note: into supplies its first two letters TO as a word

explanation.surface: A poet is taken aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquato Tasso was a sixteenth-century Italian epic poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasso wrote the epic Jerusalem Delivered, an example of the category.

clue.text: Make out notes by a person of no importance

parts.note: D and E are two musical notes
a cipher is a nonentity, a nobody

explanation.surface: Reading notes written by a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out a text is to decode or interpret it.

clue.text: The baroness's elusive plant?

parts.note: Baroness Orczy's elusive hero, the Scarlet ..., named after a small red wildflower

explanation.surface: A noblewoman's hard-to-find flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet one is a wild flower and the alias of Orczy's elusive hero.

clue.text: County arranged date for supporting the retired

parts.note: Beds is short for Bedfordshire, an English county

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the following word are reordered

explanation.surface: A county fixes a date for helping pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' means gone to bed, not pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed frame holds up those who have gone to bed.

clue.text: Cruel one about to pursue elephant crossing river

indicators.note: to pursue means the one-about letters come after the elephant
crossing means the elephant's name straddles the river letter

parts.note: Babar is the elephant of the French children's books
I is the Roman numeral one
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A savage beast chases an elephant fording a river.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into BABAR to give BARBAR, and IC follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage, uncivilised behaviour is barbaric, a synonym of brutal.

clue.text: Allowance — one accepted by teachers in any environment

indicators.note: environment means the word any surrounds the rest
accepted by means the one letter is taken inside the teachers

parts.note: NUT is the National Union of Teachers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A grant welcomed by teachers anywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: An annuity is a fixed yearly payment, a kind of allowance.

clue.text: Low points reached by ruminants

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
S and E are compass points

explanation.surface: Cattle lowing as they reach compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Moose are large deer, which chew the cud like cattle, so are examples.

clue.text: Princess wearing spectacles for seasoning the food

indicators.note: wearing means the princess is inside the spectacles

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of glasses
Regan is a princess, daughter of King Lear

explanation.surface: A royal in glasses flavours the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb used to flavour food, an example of seasoning.

clue.text: She gave advice, for instance, on going up river

parts.note: eg is for example

indicators.note: going up, in a down clue, reverses the river

parts.note: the Aire is a Yorkshire river

explanation.surface: A woman gave tips, for example, while heading upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: Egeria was the nymph who advised King Numa, so her name means a female adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria was a mythical counsellor, so her name denotes a woman adviser.

clue.text: Information given by boy concerning a class

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
Eric is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad supplies facts about a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means relating to a whole group or kind rather than a specific one.

clue.text: Bachelor leaves local office to establish farm

indicators.note: leaves means the bachelor letter departs

parts.note: a branch is a local office of a firm

explanation.surface: A single man quits the branch office to start a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle.

clue.text: Futile exploits involving the French

indicators.note: involving means the word for exploits wraps round the French article

parts.note: to exploit is to use, so exploits is uses
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Pointless deeds involving French people.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile and useless both mean having no effect, synonyms.

clue.text: Precipitation is reported to prevail

indicators.note: is reported means the word is heard rather than read, so a homophone

parts.note: rain is precipitation

explanation.surface: Weather forecasts say rain will dominate.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold sway or predominate, a synonym of prevail.

clue.text: Stupid constituents in nine seats

indicators.note: constituents in means the letters making up the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dim voters in nine parliamentary seats.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NINE SEATS are rearranged; 'constituents' looks like voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Insensate means senseless or foolish, a synonym of stupid.

clue.text: No matter what, it goes. Porter noted

explanation.surface: A permissive motto quoted from a songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: Anything Goes is a musical by Cole Porter, the American songwriter.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything means whatever at all, and Porter's song title completes the phrase.

clue.text: Nut drops ring in a Scottish loch

indicators.note: drops means a letter is taken out of the loch

parts.note: Loch Lomond is a famous Scottish loch
O looks like a ring

explanation.surface: A nut falls with a ring into a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An almond is a kind of nut, an example.
